From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Sam Tanner <sam.tanner@brightpath.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BrightPath vendor review — initial note

Hi Sam,

Thanks again for taking time on the call yesterday. I promised to follow up with a concise counter-proposal and a short technical note on where Redwood would reduce unit costs (batching + KV cache) without compromising latency. Attached: redwood-offer.pdf (short summary + sample SLA).

High-level offer:
- 12 month committed term (flexible seat usage)
- 20% list discount off published runtime rates, plus a three-month onboarding credit applied to first invoice
- Optional private deployment (VPC) add-on — separate line item

Questions I flagged from our call that I want to confirm before sending a formal quote:
1) Do you need on-prem (air-gapped) or is VPC sufficient?
2) What percentage of traffic is peak vs baseline (so we can price burst capacity properly)?
3) Any mandatory procurement/legal clauses we should pre-check (PO cadence, Net30 vs Net45)?

If you can share the BrightPath number for baseline monthly token volume and their current per-token effective price, we’ll produce a true mirror comparison (line-by-line).

If it helps, I can run a short two-hour ops workshop to validate compatibility (KV cache handoffs, egress patterns) — we’ve found a couple quick wins there that materially reduce billed tokens.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attach: redwood-offer.pdf

From: Sam Tanner <sam.tanner@brightpath.com>

Subject: Re: BrightPath vendor review — mirror pricing & ops constraints

Connor,

Appreciate the follow-up and the PDF. Quick answers below and I pasted the current BrightPath economics so you can mirror it:

- Deployment: VPC-only; on-prem is not on the table for this phase.
- Traffic profile: ~70% baseline (steady stream for inference), spikes up to 250% during batch jobs (overnight and month-end reporting).
- Procurement: Net30, standard SOW + MSSA.

Current effective: 0.00018 $/token (weighted average across generation/embedding mixture). They’ve offered a migration credit of 2 months of paid runtime if we move within next 60 days.

Two asks from my side:
1) Can you commit to parity on effective per-token economics (including credits) assuming a 12-month commit?
2) Can you provide a short ops compatibility checklist — specifically around KV cache warm-start behavior and egress accounting for streamed responses?

If you can answer the parity + ops checklist, we’ll pull procurement in and fast-track a PO.

Sam
Sam Tanner
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightPath Inc
procure@brightpath.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-30T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightPath vendor review — parity and ops checklist (internal)

Connor — attached pricing_workbook.xlsx. Quick summary of what I recommend:

- List rates: keep as standard. For BrightPath profile (70/30 embed/generate) our blended list is 0.00022 $/token.
- Concession path to match 0.00018 effective:
  * 15% baseline discount on runtime rates (applies to committed baseline usage)
  * 2-month onboarding credit applied as prepaid invoice credit (reduces first-quarter burn)
  * Technical credit: 3 months of premium support + two onsite workshops (virtual) to accelerate cache warm-starts

That combination nets to ~0.000177 effective across the first 12 months (workbook shows the math). I also included an alternative: 10% discount + extended 18-month term if they prefer longer commitment instead of credits.

Marissa — ops notes in the sheet (tab "ops_risks"):
- KV cache warm-start: we recommend a small warm-up window (10–30 minutes) after failover; can be optimized with prefix caching and a short-lived pre-warm script on their side. No on-prem code changes required.
- Streaming egress accounting: we'll bill tokens generated + streaming overhead. For housekeeping, suggest they batch the reporting jobs into 2x nightly windows to reduce peak unit-cost exposure.

I flagged the legal ask: Net30 is fine; our standard MSSA has a data retention clause they may want tweaked — loop legal if they push.

Attaches: pricing_workbook.xlsx

-Rishi
Director, Commercial Pricing
Redwood Inference

Sam — thanks for the clarity. Please find attached the formal counter: pricing_workbook.xlsx (line-by-line mirror), and a draft MSSA + SOW (signed-ma-draft.docx) for procurement to review. Highlights below: 

Counter highlights (12 month term, committed baseline + burst policy):
- Effective economics: 0.000177 $/token across the first 12 months (includes 2 months onboarding credit + 15% baseline discount). Full math in the workbook.
- Onboarding credits: two months of runtime credit applied as invoice offset; three months complimentary Premium Support (virtual workshops focused on KV cache warm-start).
- Deployment: VPC (no on-prem changes required); ops checklist attached in workbook tab "ops_risks" including recommended warm-start script and sample prefix cache config.
- Procurement: we accept Net30; draft MSSA attached for legal review.

Mutual action plan (next steps):
1) BrightPath confirms baseline committed volume (tokens/month) — we’ll update final invoice schedule (target by 10/04).
2) Procurement reviews MSSA and returns redlines (target by 10/08).
3) Ops workshop scheduled week of 10/11 (2-hour session) — we’ll share pre-read.
4) Aim for PO issuance by 10/18 and kickoff on 10/25.

Sam — we believe this gets you parity on economics while giving BrightPath the operational guardrails to avoid peak egress surprises. If this looks good I’ll route the final quote for signature.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien

Redwood Inference
